db_assertions.db_subject: Cationicity Enhancement on the Hydrophilic Face of Ctriporin Significantly Reduces Its Hemolytic Activity and Improves the Antimicrobial Activity against Antibiotic-Resistant ESKAPE Pathogens
db_assertions.db_measure: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (94.74%) to Ctriporin I=L=K: 16%, A=S: 11%. Activity: active against S. aureus ATCC29213 or ATCC25923 (MIC 8-15.9 uM), E. faecium ATCC29212 (MIC 7.7 uM), E. coli ATCC25922 or ATCC35218 (MIC 3.9-15.4 uM), P-aeruginosa ATCC27853 (MIC >30.7 uM), K. pneumoniae ATCC700603 (MIC 30.7 uM), A. baumannii ATCC19606 (MIC 3.8 uM). In vitro toxicity: human RBC: HC50 >150 ug/ml, low hemo.lytic at MIC. Structure: random coil in water and helical in 30 mM SDS micelles.

SAR: the change of P to K here reduced peptide activity compared to CM6.
